chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who entered Mecca after the Asr prayer, so he performed Tawaf by the House, and we had taught him how to pray, but he forgot, so he sat until the sun set. Then he saw the people performing Tawaf, so he stood up and performed another Tawaf before praying the two cycles for the obligatory Tawaf. He said: 'Ignorant?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.جَاهِلٌ: Ignorant (one who does not know the ruling)
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty or requirement)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray the two rak'ahs after Tawaf and is ignorant of the obligation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who, due to ignorance, omitted the two rak'ahs of Tawaf and performed an extra circumambulation before praying; he rules that no penalty is incurred. This highlights the Shia principle of leniency (*rukhsah*) for those unaware of specific ritual details, distinguishing between intentional omission and genuine ignorance (*jahil*). The hadith underscores the importance of intention and knowledge in ritual validity, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the conditions of obligatory acts.
